newsitem.title: BELGIUM: FORECAST - Belgian dealers see higher 1996 growth.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Belgian dealers see higher 1996 growth.

text.p: The 15 banks which are primary dealers in Belgian state debt have revised their forecasts for 1996 real gross domestic product (GDP) growth to 1.3 percent from 1.2 percent, they said in their Belgian Financial Newsletter on Monday.
"According to recent indicators, the recovery has spread throughout all sectors of the Belgian economy and seems to be accelerating as the year progresses," they said.

They added that, owing to its specialistion in products which play an essential role in the starting phase of a cyclical rebound, the Belgian economomy generally reacts very quickly to a revival in demand.
The European Union (EU) and the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development's (OECD) 1996 forecasts for real GDP growth are 1.1 and 1.5 percent.
For 1997 primary dealers see 2.1 percent growth, the EU sees 2.2 percent, the OECD sees 2.5 percent.
